meta.maintenanceInstruction: Single source of truth, maintained per the /blueprint-json skill. Read it whole before any work. Execute sequentialTasks in order; one task In Progress at a time. Record deviations inside the affected task. Validate with python3 -m json.tool after every edit. The file carries git skip-worktree: the disk copy is authoritative.
meta.sourceOfTruth: The source tree at HEAD plus the player-eye harness (examples/labyrinth/e2e/player/) run against a freshly built binary. Harness detector verdicts on real input are the acceptance oracle for every player-visible claim.

globalAlerts: SCOPE (Hana 2026-10-26): fix every confirmed player-visible bug AND make the game fun. Fun is proven by the fun gate (task T10) and finally by Hana's own playtest (T12). Do not stop at 'bugs fixed'.

VERIFY LIKE A PLAYER: every task's acceptance is judged by running the player-eye harness with real input (headed Chrome) and looking at the flipbooks/diary, per examples/labyrinth/docs/playtesting.md. Green unit tests alone never complete a task.

NEVER WEAKEN A DETECTOR TO GET GREEN. A detector may change only when (a) a flipbook shows it is wrong (false positive) and (b) a new case in e2e/player/player.test.mjs pins the fix, or (c) a task below explicitly changes a game rule the detector encodes (listed in that task).

ANTI-REWARD-HACKING: no test-detecting conditionals, no special-casing seeds, no fake action success, no hiding overlays or calling __ariadne debug actions in player-eye journeys (the cheat guard invalidates the run).

GO STYLE: every Go file under examples/labyrinth carries //go:build example and stays under 900 lines. game/session.go is at 870 lines: new server logic goes in NEW files named in each task (game/damage.go, game/presence.go, game/bolts.go, game/sigils.go). Zero diff to root *.go and go.mod/go.sum.
EMBED TRAP: client/ is go:embed'ed. The player-eye CLI rebuilds the binary itself; anything else (manual server, botlab) needs a rebuild after client edits. Kill servers by exact PID, never pkill.
HEADED RUNS: the player-eye harness opens a visible Chrome window with real pointer lock. Do not touch the physical mouse during a run. Runs take ~25-90 s per journey.

mandatoryDirectives.contextManagement: Cold start: read this file whole, then examples/labyrinth/docs/playtesting.md, then the files named in the current task. Do not rely on memory of code; open it.
mandatoryDirectives.taskLoop: For the current task: (1) run its RED check first and save the run dir path in the task's 'evidence' (proves the bug exists before you fix it); (2) implement exactly the listed changes; (3) update the listed tests; (4) run continuousVerification.commands; (5) run the task's GREEN check, open the flipbooks/diary it produces and confirm by eye; (6) /quality-check the task; (7) commit with a message naming the task id; (8) set status Done with evidence (run dir, detector counts, test counts).
mandatoryDirectives.designDecisions: knowledgeStore.design holds decisions already made for you. Follow them. If one proves impossible, stop, record why in the task, and replan rather than improvising a different design.
mandatoryDirectives.evidenceDiscipline: Every number written into this file must come from a command you ran. Quote the run directory for harness evidence.
mandatoryDirectives.tuning: Gameplay constants (speeds, damage, ranges, cooldowns) may be tuned freely in T10 to meet the fun bands; earlier tasks use the starting values given in knowledgeStore.design.

domainModel.elements: Fire 0 > Ice 1 > Lightning 2 > Void 3 > Fire. Advantage x2 damage, disadvantage x0.5 (game/element.go:23). Player starts Fire.
domainModel.archetypes: Brute 0 (Fire, HP 40, dmg 20, mass 3.0), Swarm 1 (Ice, 20/8/0.5), Caster 2 (Lightning, 25/12/1.0), Stalker 3 (Void, 25/15/0.8). Tables in game/session.go:80-179; ids B-/S-/C-/K- never reused.
domainModel.world: 21x21 maze (maze.Generate, main.go:61), start near (1,1), gate near (19,19). Cells: 0 wall, 1 floor, 2 platform, 3 gap. Server 30 Hz (loop/loop.go), snapshots 20 Hz. ONE shared world and ONE runner for all sessions.
domainModel.pabt: Each actor runs a PA-BT brain (brain/): goal Caught OR SearchExhausted; actions Pursue/Search/Recover/Retreat/Reinforce. Faction behaviour (patrol/raid/retreat, clashes, hazards) is game-level code in game/faction_war.go.

rootCauses: Remaining from baseline: Mobs ignore the player (Pursue stops at <0.6u; applyStrategyMovement overrides when !MovedLastTick; AllyYielding steps aside; AtDisadvantage flees at full HP) -> T7.
Blank first view: spawn yaw 0 faces a wall; walls are untextured and lit only by one directional light, so a near wall looks like the void -> T6.
Crosshair lies: aim-lock (main.mjs:639-658) has no line-of-sight test -> T6.
Gap cells look like floor but block shots and sight (rayOccluded / HasClearLOS use Walkable()) -> T6.
Actors embedded in walls (D8): maze.Resolve single pass over 3x3 cells can push a cylinder out of cell A into adjacent wall cell B when cornered during separation/clash -> T6.
End screen click ignored: pointer stays locked so the click hits the canvas -> T9.
Boring: no objective beyond walking to the gate (~15 s run), one-shot power-ups, no telegraphs, enemies busy with each other -> T7, T8, T10.

Playtesting slop: walkTo stops W on every turn >=0.45rad, J3/J4 use full-map actor coordinates invisible on screen/minimap, J2 walks into enemies without fighting or dodging, engage() acts as a stationary turret, J1 does 32 robotic look steps -> T6b.

design.D7_readability: gl.mjs fragment shader: add a camera headlamp term (1/(1+0.35*d^2)) and, for wall instances, a procedural brick/mortar pattern from vWorldPos and the face normal, selected by vColor.a < 0.5 (alpha is unused today: no blending). Walls must render clearly lighter than the clear colour at every distance under 1.5u. Spawn yaw: maze.StartYaw = yaw toward the longest open straight corridor from Start (computed in maze/maze.go), sent in the maze proto and applied by onMaze and by NewSession. Gap cells become 'rifts': rendered as a dark recessed slab with a glowing crack colour, walkable by the player, transparent to shots and sight (rayOccluded and brain HasClearLOS block on walls only), still avoided by enemy pathing (PathWalkable unchanged) so rifts are tactical refuges. Platforms render as a raised 0.15 slab. Crosshair aim-lock adds a wall-only LOS test. Multi-pass (3 iterations) in maze.Resolve + predict.mjs so cornered actors/players never end up in an adjacent wall cell.
design.D7b_human_playtesting: Enforce human-like playtesting and decrease slop recurrence via 4 layers: (1) Perception boundary in inpage.mjs __pe.read(): filter returned actors to those within minimap/radar awareness (<=6.5u) or on-screen LOS (<=15u and wall-clear LOS), while keeping full actors in pe.samples for post-hoc detectors. (2) Smooth locomotion & kiting in pilot.mjs: walkTo holds W continuously through turns up to 1.15rad (only releasing W when facing a wall <0.7u at >1.0rad error), uses A/D strafe for corridor alignment, and supports reactive combat/evasion when enemies block the corridor; engage() strafes/backs up (S/A/D) to maintain standoff distance (1.8-4.5u) while aiming and firing instead of standing still as a turret; faceYaw uses smooth multi-step mouse glides. (3) Realistic journeys in journeys.mjs: J1 uses natural sweeping looks (6-8 varied turns across the corridor and walls) instead of 32 identical ticks; J2 defends itself or evades when an enemy blocks its corridor on the way to the gate; J3/J4 explore corridors/quadrants to find enemies within perception range rather than reading full-map coordinates. (4) Anti-slop detector D19 (detectPilotRealism in control.mjs) + diary metrics: flags S2 if the pilot exhibits stop-and-go W-churn (>2.5 W-releases/s during navigation), stationary turret combat (<20% time moving during >=3s of close combat), whip-turn spikes (>18 rad/s mouse snap), or targets an unperceivable actor.
design.D8_enemy_combat: Engagement: applyStrategyMovement yields whenever the brain is engaged (player detected or caught), not only when it moved. Pursue keeps closing to AttackRange 0.85 and never parks. Remove player-directed AllyYielding (same-element mobs are hostile). AtDisadvantage triggers retreat only when the actor's HP < 60%. Melee is telegraphed: an actor within AttackRange starts a windup (WindupTicks 12 = 0.4 s, Minotaur.Windup field, snapshot field 'atk' 0..1); at windup end, if still within 1.1u, damageRunner + knockRunner(0.5u); cooldown 45 ticks. Casters: per-caster cooldown 75 ticks, windup 15 ticks, then spawn a server bolt projectile (game/bolts.go: pos, vel 7 u/s, radius 0.25, ttl 2 s) that damages on contact and dies on walls; bolts go in the snapshot and the client draws them. Gunshots alert every actor within 10u (sets LastKnownPos = player). Gun hit knockback stays server-side and is now visible because rendering follows the server.
design.D9_objective: Sigils: 4 sigils, one per faction quadrant, placed with homeTerritoryPos far from Start (game/sigils.go). The gate is locked (red) until 3 sigils are carried; then it turns green. Picking a sigil: intensity +1, and that faction hunts the player for 12 s (every actor of that element gets LastKnownPos = player and Raid toward the player); banner 'THE EMBER LEGION HUNTS YOU'. Power-ups respawn 45 s after pickup. Escalation spawns stop growing the roster beyond TargetActorCount+2. Win stats: time, sigils, kills, damage taken, shots, accuracy.
design.D10_end_restart: On caught/win: document.exitPointerLock(), send play off, show the stats overlay with the killer ('Slain by Ember Legion Brute') or the win time and best time (localStorage, try/catch). Restart by click, Enter or R: location.reload() (the server resets the terminal world on rejoin). The tutorial is not shown again in the same tab.
design.D11_fun_bands: Fun gate bands, measured by J6 over 5 seeds (DESIGN values; change only with Hana's approval recorded in replanFocus): time to first enemy on screen <= 25 s; enemy on screen 30-75% of play; longest dead time <= 15 s; on-screen enemies standing still <= 35%; server mobs that see the player close in >= 60%; HP lost to never-seen enemies <= 10%; silent damage 0; every melee hit telegraphed (D18) 100%; pilot wins 2-4 of 5 seeds; median J6 run 120-360 s; >= 3 archetypes engaged per run; >= 1 visible faction clash within 8u of the player per run.

playerEye.what: examples/labyrinth/e2e/player/: real-input, screen-judged harness. Journeys J1 cold start+controls, J2 run to gate+play again, J3 combat, J4 death+restart, J5 alt-tab/resize/Escape/reload, J6 full run (T8). Detectors D1-D19 (docs/playtesting.md). Outputs per journey: findings.json, flipbooks/, filmstrip.png, video.mp4, diary.md. --analyze <journeyDir>, --rejudge <runDir>. Self-tests: node --test examples/labyrinth/e2e/player/*.test.mjs.
playerEye.baseline: Pre-fix evidence (3 seeds x J1-J5): examples/labyrinth/e2e/artifacts/player/2026-10-26/findings.md. Every confirmed bug in rootCauses reproduced there.
playerEye.traps: Real pointer lock needs page.bringToFront() right before the click (lockPointer does it). | Playwright fakes focus; J5 disables Emulation focus emulation around alt-tab to get a real blur. | Screencast emits frames only on change: the screen at time t is the last frame at or before t (FrameStore.at). | Pixel-shift estimates need HUD masks and gestures whose expected shift fits +-120px. | Journey marks can share a millisecond: order by array index. | Presence metrics use the enemy's own displacement, not the closing distance.

sequentialTasks.task: T10: Fun gate and balance pass
sequentialTasks.description: Implements design.D11_fun_bands. Steps: (1) e2e/player: add --gate fun to playtest-player.mjs: runs J6 on the given seeds and computes every band in D11 from the timelines (reuse feelProfile, serverPresence, D13/D18/D19 numbers; add time-to-first-enemy, run length, archetypes engaged, nearby clashes); writes fun-gate.md with each band PASS/FAIL and exits 1 on any FAIL. Unit-test the band computation on synthetic timelines. (2) Tune constants (actorSpeed, damage tables, AttackRange, windup/cooldowns, sight range, TargetActorCount, power-up and regen timings, sigil placement distance) until the gate passes on seeds 12345,777,4242,31337,2024. Record each tuning step (constant, old -> new, which band moved) in this task's evidence. (3) The J6 pilot is the reference player: do not change its skill, aim, routing or timing to pass a band; only fix pilot bugs, each with a recorded reason. (4) Keep all other detectors (D1-D19) at zero S1/S2.
sequentialTasks.acceptance: cd examples/labyrinth && node e2e/player/playtest-player.mjs --seed 12345,777,4242,31337,2024 --gate fun --out <dir> exits 0 twice in a row on fresh runs, and fun-gate.md shows every band PASS with its number; the J6 diaries read as a coherent run (explore, fight, hunted, escape or die) when read cold.
sequentialTasks.evidence: fungate.mjs and fungate.test.mjs implemented and verified (node --test: 3/3 pass; all 49 e2e/player tests pass). Next: wire --gate fun into playtest-player.mjs, run J6 on 5 seeds, tune constants.

sequentialTasks.task: T11: Full verification, review and documentation
sequentialTasks.description: Steps: (1) Run every continuousVerification command. (2) cd examples/labyrinth && node e2e/player/playtest-player.mjs --seed 12345,777,4242,31337,2024 --journeys J1,J2,J3,J4,J5,J6 --keep-frames --out <dir>: zero S1/S2 findings across D1-D19. (3) Do the full playtesting.md protocol yourself: answer the 7-question charter for every journey with frame citations. (4) Independent AI playtest panel: three fresh reviewer subagents each read the J6 diaries and filmstrips of 5 seeds cold and score Readability, Controls, Threat, Fairness, Goal clarity, Pacing (1-5) with justifications; any score below 3 or any blocker is a new task. (5) Update docs: playtesting.md (J6, D18, D19, --gate fun), tutorial text, a short examples/labyrinth/docs/gameplay.md describing the loop, controls and the design bands. (6) /quality-check over the whole change set; fix and re-verify. (7) Commit.
sequentialTasks.acceptance: All commands green; zero S1/S2 across 5 seeds x J1-J6; every panel score >= 3 and mean >= 3.5 with no blockers; docs describe the game as it now plays; quality-check clean.

sequentialTasks.description: Hand over: give Hana the build command (go run -tags example ./examples/labyrinth -seed 12345), the gameplay.md summary, and the latest fun-gate.md. Record her feedback verbatim (paraphrase nothing) in replanFocus. Any problem she raises becomes new tasks via the Replan protocol, each with a detector or test that reproduces it before it is fixed.
sequentialTasks.acceptance: Hana states the game is fun and the reported issues are resolved. Until then this task stays Not Started/In Progress.

continuousVerification.failurePolicy: A task is not Done while any command above fails, while its GREEN check shows its target detectors on any of the 3 seeds, or while a flipbook shows a player-visible problem the detectors missed (add a detector or test for it first). Exception: a failure listed in knownFailures that is proven pre-existing at the task's base commit and assigned to a later task does not block the current task, but it must stay recorded until fixed.
